title: Wisent failure envelope
description: One shape for every failure any Wisent component reports. The fields answer, in order, the questions an operator asks: where did it break, what kind of failure is it, whose fault, is it worth retrying, and what exactly did the layer below say.

failure_point.description: Three dotted segments: <service>.<surface>.<operation>. The one field that makes a failure findable in source.

error_code.description: One of the catalogue's codes. Never a free-form string: a code nobody can look up is a sentence, not a classification.

service.description: The product that emitted this, as the fleet names it.

impact.description: What the caller lost. Free text, because the blast radius of a failure is not a taxonomy.

severity.description: Derived from the code, never chosen at the call site.

retryable.description: Derived from the code. Worth running the same thing again, unchanged.

outage.description: Derived from the code. Our side is broken, as opposed to the request being wrong.

detail.description: What the layer below actually said, verbatim and truncated, never paraphrased. Required: a failure reported without its reason is the defect this schema exists to prevent.

cause.description: The failure underneath this one. A gateway refusing a request because a provider refused a token because a vault refused a read is three failures, and flattening them to the outermost is how the reason gets lost.

context.description: Identifiers a reader needs to find the subject: a host, a subscription id, a job. Values are scalars so a log shipper can index them.
